data.body:
GAP-FILL — the b690 stretch was under-recorded HERE (it is fully recorded on b690, but this log is the cross-ticket trail and three substantive items never reached it). Audited on request; closing the gap rather than claiming the log was complete.

**b690 (story, parented to 061c, CERTIFIED, CLAIMED) took FIVE plan-review rounds.** R1 PASSED first-time; then the operator reclassified it bug->story and required observability first, which was a MATERIAL edit that voided the attestation. R2 BLOCK: an external-evidence AC missing [operator-attested]. R3 BLOCK x4, all one root: I had added Step 0's files to `file_impact` but not to the Scope PROSE, so the two disagreed. R4 BLOCK x2: I specified how the STEP ID reaches the log but left the identical problem unspecified for the CLASS TOKEN. R5 PASS. Every block was an item already on my own checklist — the checks only help when run BEFORE submitting.

**STEP 0 = OBSERVABILITY FIRST (the operator's call, and it was the right one).** `usage_log.record()` stores `op` = the PROMPT NAME and nothing identifying the caller, and `code-review-base` is the prompt used by BOTH the `base` step and the `round_a`/`round_b` batch finder — so no record can be attributed to a step, and every diagnosis on top of it is a guess. Step 0 adds `step` + `model_class` (the latter only when the raw token is in `CLASS_NAMES`). DESIGN DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT: `RunRequest` is constructed at **25 sites**, most with no step context, so a new field was rejected (required churns 25; optional leaves ~24 passing None) and overloading `target` was rejected as semantic abuse — chose a **ContextVar** set by the step executor, mirroring the existing `_active_gate_config` precedent at `llm/config.py:88`.
The class token needs the SAME carrier: by `runner.py:547` the class is GONE (`resolve_model` collapsed it; `resolve_model_string` returns a bare string), and reverse lookup is UNSOUND because two classes may resolve to the same model. Widening `resolve_model_string` to a tuple was rejected on a checked fact — SEVEN call sites consume its string.

**TWO MORE HYPOTHESES ELIMINATED BY EXPERIMENT** (cumulative total five): the v3 migration does NOT strip the declarations (identical before/after `migrate_to_current`), and the running package loads MY gate copy. Still merely a SUSPECT, deliberately not acted on: `config.py:211` resolves with no `repo_root` while the live run sits inside `gate_source.gate_read_root(handle)` — and it cannot be the whole story, because a fallback class table would give `verify` SONNET and the log showed OPUS.

**THE TEST'S CAPTURE POINT, and a trap that would have produced a worthless green test.** Capture at `runs.py:236` `get_runner(cfg, override=self._runner)` -> `:261` `runner.run(req)`, where `req.config.model` is the POST-resolution value. The trap: the existing offline harness (`tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_workflow.py:402`) passes `agent_runner=_FakeRunner(...)`, which REPLACES `RunnerAgentStep` and never runs `resolve_model` — a recording runner built that way passes while proving only what 3768's tests already proved. The fake must sit BENEATH the production agent step. And because `RunRequest` carries no step id, the offline fake needs the SAME ContextVar as the live log — independent confirmation that Step 0 is a prerequisite, not polish.
